args.title: checkout-api rolled back to v2.3.0 after health check failures
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (error rate ~18%). Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. First rollback attempt hit a partial failure (orchestrator error after us-east), so a second rollback was issued; all regions now report v2.3.0 and healthy (error rate ~0.2%).

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I've completed the task:

1. **Diagnosed the issue**: `checkout-api` was running `v2.3.1` in all regions, unhealthy with an ~18% error rate.

2. **Identified the rollback target**: The most recent healthy production release was `v2.3.0` (v2.3.1 was unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only).

3. **Rolled back**: The first rollback attempt hit a partial failure (orchestrator error after `us-east`), leaving a mixed state. I re-issued the rollback, which completed successfully — all regions (`us-east`, `us-west`, `eu-west`) are now on `v2.3.0`, healthy, with error rate back down to ~0.2%.

4. **Opened a SEV2 incident**: The `create_incident` call timed out, but I verified via `list_incidents` that the incident was actually created — `INC-0001`, SEV2, open, describing the rollback and the partial-failure retry.
